facetTint.purpose: Lightness and chroma per theme; each card supplies only --facet-hue, so contrast is guaranteed in both themes.

display.purpose: The rolled sentence only; balanced wrap, two lines reserved (three under 640px).

title.purpose: A compartment's name, beside its checkbox.

body.purpose: Chip labels (500) and general interface text (400).

label.purpose: Card hints, reveal toggle, theme options, footer.

shadows.name: compartment
shadows.purpose: Light theme only: cards and the result banner resting on paper. Dark theme sets --shadow: none and separates tonally.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Hover and control state on buttons, options, chips.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Button :active; resets the instant the pointer lifts.

motion.name: theme-crossfade
motion.purpose: Theme switch on html/body and surfaces; 120ms under reduced motion.

motion.name: land
motion.purpose: A locked chip dropping into its row; becomes a 180ms opacity appear under reduced motion.

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: The sentence re-keying as each slot locks; a settle, not an entrance.

motion.name: reveal-slide
motion.purpose: Card controls and chips entering or leaving when a facet is armed; 150ms fade under reduced motion.

motion.name: rattle
motion.purpose: The dice rattle per slot; skippable by button, Escape, or the persisted toggle.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single action on screen: Roll everything.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { font: inherit; font-weight: 600; background: var(--accent, #6ea8fe); color: var(--accent-text, #0b1526); border: 1px solid var(--accent, #6ea8fe); border-radius: 8px; padding: 0.45rem 0.9rem; min-height: 2.5rem; cursor: pointer; transition: background .15s, border-color .15s, color .15s, transform .1s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { filter: brightness(1.1); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #6ea8fe); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.97); transition-duration: .05s; }

components.name: Default Button
components.description: Per-card Roll and the reveal Skip.
components.css: .ds-btn { font: inherit; color: var(--text, #e8eaed); background: var(--chip, #242a31); border: 1px solid var(--border, #2e353d); border-radius: 8px; padding: 0.45rem 0.9rem; min-height: 2.5rem; cursor: pointer; transition: background .15s, border-color .15s, color .15s, transform .1s; } .ds-btn:hover { border-color: var(--accent, #6ea8fe); } .ds-btn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #6ea8fe); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn:active { transform: scale(0.97); transition-duration: .05s; } .ds-btn:disabled { opacity: .5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Result Chip
components.description: A rolled result, tinted with its facet's hue so it traces back to its card.

components.name: Described Chip
components.description: A result carrying a description (master plots).
components.html: The HeistA plan, a crew and a prize — and every step has to land in order.
components.css: .ds-chip-desc { --tint-bg: oklch(var(--tint-bg-l, 30%) var(--tint-bg-c, .045) var(--facet-hue)); --tint-border: oklch(var(--tint-border-l, 46%) var(--tint-border-c, .09) var(--facet-hue)); --tint-text: oklch(var(--tint-text-l, 92%) var(--tint-text-c, .03) var(--facet-hue)); --tint-muted: oklch(var(--tint-muted-l, 78%) var(--tint-muted-c, .05) var(--facet-hue)); display: inline-flex; flex-direction: column; gap: .15rem; max-width: 28rem; background: var(--tint-bg); border: 1px solid var(--tint-border); color: var(--tint-text); border-radius: 12px; padding: .5rem .9rem; } .ds-chip-desc-label { font-weight: 500; } .ds-chip-desc-body { font-size: .8rem; line-height: 1.35; color: var(--tint-muted); }

components.name: Ghost Chip
components.description: A decoy shown while a slot is rattling: dashed, blurred, fixed width so the rattle cannot reflow the row.
components.css: .ds-chip-ghost { display: inline-flex; width: 7.5rem; max-width: 100%; background: var(--chip, #242a31); color: var(--muted, #9aa3ad); border: 1px dashed var(--border, #2e353d); border-radius: 999px; padding: .35rem .8rem; filter: blur(.6px); } .ds-chip-ghost-label { white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-chip-ghost { filter: none; } }

components.name: Facet Card
components.description: One compartment of the tray: checkbox, title, hint, count, Roll, and its results. Becomes a row at 720px.
components.html: What kind of game it is
components.css: .ds-card { display: grid; gap: .75rem; background: var(--surface, #1b1f24); border: 1px solid var(--border, #2e353d); border-radius: 12px; box-shadow: var(--shadow, none); padding: 1rem 1.25rem; transition: border-color .15s, background-color .25s ease-out, padding .22s ease-out; } .ds-card-head { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: .2rem; } .ds-card-title { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: .5rem; font-weight: 600; font-size: 1.05rem; min-height: 2.75rem; margin-block: -.5rem; cursor: pointer; } .ds-card-check { width: 1.1rem; height: 1.1rem; margin: 0; accent-color: oklch(var(--tint-accent-l, 75%) var(--tint-accent-c, .14) var(--facet-hue)); } .ds-card-hint { margin: 0; color: var(--muted, #9aa3ad); font-size: .85rem; } .ds-card-controls { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: .75rem; flex-wrap: wrap; } .ds-card-count { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: .5rem; font-size: .9rem; color: var(--muted, #9aa3ad); } .ds-card-range { font-size: .8rem; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }

components.name: Number Field
components.description: How many results a facet rolls; recessed against the card, tabular numerals, snapped back into bounds on change.
components.html: <input type="number" inputmode="numeric" value="2" min="1" max="4" class="ds-input-number">
components.css: .ds-input-number { font: inherit; width: 4rem; color: var(--text, #e8eaed); background: var(--bg, #121417); border: 1px solid var(--border, #2e353d); border-radius: 6px; padding: .25rem .4rem; min-height: 2.25rem; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-input-number:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #6ea8fe); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-input-number:disabled { opacity: .6; } @media (pointer: coarse) { .ds-input-number { min-height: 2.75rem; } }

components.name: Theme Switcher
components.description: The only persistent control: a pill-shaped segmented group of System / Light / Dark over visually hidden radios.
components.css: .ds-toggle { display: inline-flex; gap: .15rem; margin: 0; padding: .2rem; border: 1px solid var(--border, #2e353d); border-radius: 999px; background: var(--surface, #1b1f24); } .ds-toggle-option { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; padding: .3rem .8rem; min-height: 2rem; border-radius: 999px; font-size: .85rem; color: var(--muted, #9aa3ad); cursor: pointer; user-select: none; transition: background .15s, color .15s; } .ds-toggle-option:hover { color: var(--text, #e8eaed); } .ds-toggle-option.ds-is-active { background: var(--chip, #242a31); color: var(--text, #e8eaed); font-weight: 600; } @media (pointer: coarse) { .ds-toggle-option { min-height: 2.5rem; } }

components.name: Result Banner
components.description: The reading surface: composed sentence at display size with two lines reserved, primary action, and the reveal toggle.
components.html: A 3D online co-op puzzle platformer game about rebirth
components.css: .ds-banner { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 1rem; background: var(--surface, #1b1f24); border: 1px solid var(--border, #2e353d); border-radius: 12px; box-shadow: var(--shadow, none); padding: 1.5rem; transition: border-color .2s, background-color .25s ease-out; } .ds-banner-sentence { margin: 0; font-size: clamp(1.4rem, 3.5vw, 2rem); font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.3; min-height: 2.6em; text-wrap: balance; overflow-wrap: anywhere; } .ds-banner-line { display: inline-block; animation: ds-settle 260ms cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1); } @keyframes ds-settle { from { transform: translateY(.18em); opacity: .4; } to { transform: none; opacity: 1; } } .ds-banner-actions { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: .5rem; flex-wrap: wrap; } .ds-banner-reveal { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: .5rem; margin-inline-start: auto; font-size: .9rem; color: var(--muted, #9aa3ad); min-height: 2.5rem; cursor: pointer; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-banner-line { animation: none; } }

narrative.overview:
Game Roller is a felt-lined tray with five compartments. You arm the compartments you care about, tip the tray, and the dice rattle, slow, and settle one at a time. The sentence at the top is what the dice read when they stop. Everything in the interface is either a die, a compartment, or the reading — there is no chrome that is none of those.

The tray is quiet. Surfaces are unadorned rectangles with a single hairline border; the only saturated colour on screen is the primary action and the chips that a roll actually produced. Density is deliberate: on a wide screen each facet becomes one horizontal row — controls on the left, results pushed to the right edge — so the whole set of compartments scans as a short list rather than a page of cards to read. Motion carries weight, never decoration: a rattle that eases from 60ms to 220ms per tick, a chip that drops 0.5rem and lands with a 320ms exponential ease-out, a card that slides its controls away when you disarm it. Nothing pulses, floats, or shimmers at rest.

Dark is the room the tray sits in by default; light is a separate, composed daytime version — warm paper, white compartments, soft shadow — not the dark theme inverted. Both are first-class, and the system never assumes one.
keyCharacteristics: Five facet hues, each owned by one compartment, carried into every artifact that compartment produces
Reserved space over reflow: a landing chip never pushes the layout
One authored motion moment (the reveal) with a first-class skip
Flat tonal dark, softly shadowed light — both composed, neither inverted
System sans throughout; hierarchy comes from weight, size, and colour, never from a second face

rules.name: The Traceability Rule
rules.body: A facet hue exists so that a chip can be traced back to the compartment that produced it. A new facet earns a hue because it needs identity in the results, never because the palette wants more variety. Hues are never reused across facets and never applied to anything that is not a result, a result's control, or a live slot's edge.

rules.name: The One Action Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue marks the thing to press and the thing being interacted with — primary button, focus ring, live-reveal border, selection, caret. A second saturated element competing for the eye in the neutral shell is a bug.

rules.name: The Composed Theme Rule
rules.body: Light is authored, not derived. Warm paper (#f3f1ec), true white compartments, and real shadows; dark is cool slate, shadowless, tonal. Adding a token means choosing both values deliberately — never invert(), never a filter.

rules.name: The One Face Rule
rules.body: The system sans is the whole type system. No display face, no mono costume for "technical" — tabular numerals handle the only place numbers need to align.

rules.name: The Reserved Line Rule
rules.body: Any text that changes while the user watches reserves its height first. The sentence reserves two lines (three on mobile); chips reserve their rows once a roll exists. Text arriving must never move text already read.

rules.name: The Reserved Space Rule
rules.body: A compartment reserves exactly the height its declared count of results will occupy — --rows × --row, where --row is 2.4rem, or 5.2rem for facets whose chips carry descriptions — but only once something has been rolled. Nothing rolled means nothing can shift, and an untouched card stays closed up.

rules.name: The No-Lift Rule
rules.body: Nothing rises on hover. State is reported by border colour (hairline → Signal Blue), by a 0.97 scale press that resets the instant the pointer lifts, and by the facet hue appearing on a live card's edge. Elevation is a property of the theme's material, not a response to the cursor.

rules.name: The Skippable Reveal Rule
rules.body: The rattle is the product's one authored motion moment — ~1.5s per slot, ticks easing 60ms → 220ms, 220ms between slots — and it is always escapable: a Skip button, the Escape key, and a persisted "Reveal one by one" toggle. Motion that cannot be skipped is a cost the user did not agree to.

rules.name: The Reduced-Motion Dialect Rule
rules.body: Reduced motion swaps vocabulary, it never mutes the system: slide becomes fade, the chip landing becomes an opacity appear, the sentence settle becomes a fade, the rattle drops to a paced pending state. Hover, press, and theme cross-fade survive, because they report state. A blanket transition-duration: 0 across the document is forbidden.

dos: Do give every new facet its own OKLCH hue angle via --facet-hue, and let the theme-level --tint-*-l/c tokens supply lightness and chroma so contrast holds in both themes.
Do reserve space for anything that will arrive — --rows × --row on chips, min-height on the sentence — and only once the content can actually appear.
Do compose both theme values deliberately when adding a colour token; dark is tonal and shadowless, light is warm paper with the two-part shadow.
Do keep hierarchy in weight, size, and the reading/aside colour split, using the system sans for everything.
Do give every new motion a reduced-motion counterpart that preserves the state change (fade or an instant end state), and make any sequence longer than a second escapable.
Do report state through border colour, the 0.97 press, and hue on a live edge.
Do size touch targets through @media (pointer: coarse) rather than by changing the desktop rhythm.
donts: Don't use a facet hue for anything that is not a result, a result's own control, or a live slot's edge. It is a traceability device, not a palette.
Don't introduce a second saturated accent, a gradient fill, gradient text, or a second type face.
Don't add a shadow to the dark theme, or a hover lift to either theme. Depth belongs to the material, not the cursor.
Don't derive one theme from the other with invert(), a filter, or opacity over a light base.
Don't let arriving content push read content: no unreserved chip rows, no growing banner.
Don't kill all transitions under prefers-reduced-motion; swap the vocabulary instead.
Don't let an icon stand in for a label; the facet icon is aria-hidden and always sits beside its title text.
Don't make the rolled sentence a live region — a paced reveal in a live region reads every partial state aloud.
